# Tokens

Every token of the system, a section per group: Surfaces — 4 tokens; Text — 5 tokens; Fills and status backgrounds — 4 tokens; Palette ramps and brand — 33 tokens; Type styles, families, font files; Spacing — 7 tokens; Radius — 10 tokens; Shadow — 7 tokens; Blur — 2 tokens; Size — 20 tokens.

## Color · Surfaces

### Use

```css
/* in a page’s CSS, in the neutral theme: the token’s name, with its value from the same row of the table below as the fallback, so the page draws whether or not it links tokens.css */
color: var(--ground, #0b0c0e);
/* a page in another theme: link or inline tokens.css, put data-theme="midnight" or "warm" or "forest" or "oled" or "porcelain" on the element that wraps the page, and take each fallback from that theme’s column; where tokens.css cannot be linked, the value alone, from that theme’s column */
color: var(--ground, #090b10);   /* the midnight theme’s value */
/* on a slide, in a chart’s options, or anywhere else var() cannot go, and in an SVG attribute such as fill, which not every browser reads var() in: the value alone, from the column of the theme it is in */
color: #0b0c0e;
```

### Tokens (4)

| token | neutral | midnight | warm | forest | oled | porcelain | usage |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--ground` | #0b0c0e | #090b10 | #0e0c0a | #090d0b | #000000 | #ebebee | The window background, the darkest layer. Also the ink on the primary button and on the unread badge. Palette.ground. Porcelain makes it a pale grey (#ebebee): the one light palette. |
| `--ground-glow` | #1c1d20 | #172033 | #221c17 | #16231c | #111113 | #f8f8fa | Centre of the radial glow behind every screen (at 120,0, radius 1400 px, fading to ground). The only place a palette shows its hue. |
| `--surface` | #15161a | #121722 | #181512 | #121a16 | #0c0c0e | #ffffff | Material surface: dialogs, menus and other solid panels that sit on the ground. |
| `--surface-raised` | #1d1e23 | #1a2130 | #211d19 | #19231e | #141417 | #f3f3f5 | A cover's placeholder while it loads or when there is none; Material surfaceVariant. |

## Type

Set text in one of the styles below: write its values from the Styles and Families tables, or, on a page that links or inlines tokens.css, prefer its variable, where the Styles table’s CSS column gives one.

### Use

```css
/* any surface: a style’s values from the Styles and Families tables */
font: 700 32px/38px Inter, "Segoe UI", system-ui, sans-serif; letter-spacing: -0.6px;
/* a page that links or inlines tokens.css: prefer the variables, so that a change to tokens.css reaches the page */
font: var(--text-display-small); letter-spacing: -0.6px;
font-family: var(--font-sans);   /* the family alone */
```

### Font files

Fonts: `tokens.css` loads each font from its file, by path.

- **Design canvas:** copy `fonts/Inter-Regular.otf`, `fonts/Inter-Medium.otf`, `fonts/Inter-SemiBold.otf` and `fonts/Inter-Bold.otf` to the same paths under the canvas’s `project/ds/<folder>/` (`<folder>` is the folder you install this system under; `fonts/Inter-Regular.otf` lands on `project/ds/<folder>/fonts/Inter-Regular.otf`), in the same call that installs this system; the copy of `tokens.css` that each artboard links loads them from there. If the install’s reply leaves a font out, bring that font in as for any other page.
- **Slides deck:** for each family you use in the deck (`faces` holds at most the number of typefaces Slides’ `deck-files.md` gives), install its file with the system and name the path it lands on as that family’s `src` in `project/deck.json` `faces`, under the key in the Slides column. A deck takes a font as a file only under the rule in Slides’ `fonts.md` (no space or leading underscore in its path, for two): any other font, or one kept by id, is uploaded as `fonts.md` says.
- **Any other page:** one file per family is enough (below: the upright face nearest regular weight; bold and italic synthesize). Fetch it as the fetch column says (Artifact tool `read`, that id or path as `path`), upload it as an asset (`publish`, `file_path`, `asset:true`) and declare it with an `@font-face { font-family: "<family>"; src: url(<uploaded>) }` rule.

`tokens.css` carries the `@font-face` rules for a page that links it and names each family by the CSS variable below.

| family | file | fetch | CSS | Slides `faces` key |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Inter | `fonts/Inter-Regular.otf` (weight 400) | `read` the file with `project/` in front | `var(--font-sans)` | `inter` |

Every face: `fonts/Inter-Regular.otf` (Inter, 400), `fonts/Inter-Medium.otf` (Inter, 500), `fonts/Inter-SemiBold.otf` (Inter, 600), `fonts/Inter-Bold.otf` (Inter, 700).

## Spacing

Space in Theme.kt. Components also use 6, 10 and 14 px inline (gaps and pill padding); those are not tokens in the source.

### Use

```css
/* any surface: a token’s value from the table below */
padding: 4px;
/* a page that links or inlines tokens.css: prefer the token’s name, so that a change to tokens.css reaches the page */
padding: var(--space-xs);
```

### Tokens (7)

| token | value | usage |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--space-xs` | 4px | Segmented track padding, gap between a field label and its box. |
| `--space-sm` | 8px | Caption inset inside a title card, gap in state messages. |
| `--space-md` | 12px | Banner gaps, tri-state chip side padding, text field padding. |
| `--space-lg` | 16px | Banner side padding, gap between columns in result rows and between a shelf title and its switch. |
| `--space-xl` | 24px | Gaps between sections inside a screen. |
| `--space-xxl` | 32px | Screen side inset; shelves scroll edge to edge inside it. |
| `--space-3xl` | 48px | Gap between a widget card's header row and its body. |
